steps.title: Choose the correct question.
steps.prompt: Ask about your brother’s job.
steps.answer: What does your brother do?
steps.why: Present Simple questions: do / does + subject + infinitive.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: I can’t stand ___ in a queue.
steps.answer: waiting
steps.why: like, love, don’t mind, can’t stand are followed by -ing.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: Be quiet — the baby ___ in the next room.
steps.answer: is sleeping
steps.why: Something happening now takes the Present Continuous.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: While I ___ home, I saw an accident.
steps.answer: was driving
steps.why: The longer background action takes the Past Continuous.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: There isn’t ___ milk in the fridge.
steps.answer: much
steps.why: Milk is uncountable, so it takes much.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: This is ___ film I have ever seen.
steps.answer: the best
steps.why: A superlative takes the: the best.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: Have you finished the report ___?
steps.answer: yet
steps.why: yet goes at the end of questions and negatives.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: I ___ swim when I was five.
steps.answer: could
steps.why: Ability in the past: could.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: This bread ___ every morning.
steps.answer: is made
steps.why: The passive: be + past participle.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.after: goes to the gym before work.
steps.why: An adverb of frequency goes before the main verb.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.why: decide is followed by to + infinitive.

steps.why: an before a vowel sound, and the umbrella is not a known one.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.after: my keys, so I can’t get into the house.
steps.why: A past action with a result now takes the Present Perfect.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.after: phoned while you were out, but they didn’t leave a name.
steps.why: A positive sentence about one unknown person takes somebody.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.why: First conditional: if + Present Simple, will in the other half.

steps.title: Complete the sentence.
steps.why: A point in time takes since.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Which sentence talks about a fixed arrangement in your diary?
options: I’m seeing the dentist at four o’clock tomorrow.
I see the dentist at four o’clock tomorrow.
I will seeing the dentist at four o’clock tomorrow.
steps.answer: I’m seeing the dentist at four o’clock tomorrow.
steps.why: An arrangement already made takes the Present Continuous.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It might rain later, so take a coat.
It might to rain later, so take a coat.
It might raining later, so take a coat.
steps.answer: It might rain later, so take a coat.
steps.why: might is followed by the bare infinitive.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It’s Sunday — you don’t have to get up early.
It’s Sunday — you don’t have get up early.
It’s Sunday — you haven’t to get up early.
steps.answer: It’s Sunday — you don’t have to get up early.
steps.why: don’t have to = it is not necessary.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I had more time, I would learn the guitar.
If I would have more time, I would learn the guitar.
If I have more time, I would learn the guitar.
steps.answer: If I had more time, I would learn the guitar.
steps.why: Second conditional: if + Past Simple, would in the other half.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I used to live in Astana, but now I live here.
I use to live in Astana, but now I live here.
I used live in Astana, but now I live here.
steps.answer: I used to live in Astana, but now I live here.
steps.why: used to + infinitive for a past habit that has stopped.

steps.title: Choose the correct sentence.
steps.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I called the company to ask about the job.
I called the company for ask about the job.
I called the company for to ask about the job.
steps.answer: I called the company to ask about the job.
steps.why: The infinitive of purpose: to + infinitive.

steps.title: Find the mistake.
steps.answer: I went to the cinema last night.
steps.why: go is irregular: the past is went.

steps.title: Find the mistake.
steps.answer: I’ll call you as soon as I arrive.
steps.why: After when, as soon as, before, until English uses a present form, not will.

steps.title: Find the mistake.
steps.answer: Learning a new language takes a lot of time.
steps.why: A verb used as the subject takes the -ing form.

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: The money of another country is its ___.
steps.answer: currency

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: The papers you get when you finish a course are your ___.
steps.answer: qualifications

steps.title: Choose the correct word.
steps.prompt: Food that has not been cooked is ___.
steps.answer: raw

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: You are lost and you want the railway station.
options: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?
Where is station, please tell me it?
Say me the way of the station.
steps.answer: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: “Do you fancy going to the cinema on Friday?” You are busy on Friday.
options: I’d love to, but I’m afraid I can’t make Friday.
No. I am busy on Friday.
steps.answer: I’d love to, but I’m afraid I can’t make Friday.

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: You don’t know the English word for the thing you cook rice in.
options: It’s a kind of pan that you use for cooking rice.
Sorry, I don’t know this word.
How do you say a rice thing?
steps.answer: It’s a kind of pan that you use for cooking rice.

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: The speaker is going too fast for you.
options: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly, please?
steps.answer: Sorry, could you say that again more slowly, please?

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: Your friend says they can’t sleep. Give advice.
options: You should have an early night.
You should to have an early night.
You must to have an early night.
steps.answer: You should have an early night.

steps.title: Choose the best thing to say.
steps.prompt: Your soup arrives cold. What do you say to the waiter?
options: Excuse me, I’m afraid this soup is cold.
This soup is bad. Change it.
steps.answer: Excuse me, I’m afraid this soup is cold.

steps.title: Anna’s second start
steps.html:
From a careers blog

Anna Petrova is thirty-four and she lives in Almaty. Six years ago she worked in a large open-plan office as an accountant. “I used to spend eight hours a day with numbers,” she says. “I was good at it, but I wasn’t happy.”

In 2021 she left the company and started a small bakery with her sister. The first year was very hard. They didn’t have enough money and they worked seven days a week. “I have never been so tired in my life,” Anna says.

Things are better now. The bakery has been open for four years and it has six employees. Anna is currently studying business online in the evenings. Next spring she is going to open a second shop near the university.

“I don’t earn more than I used to,” she says, “but I love going to work.”

steps.title: Read again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: Why did Anna leave her first job?
options: She was not happy in it.
She could not do the work.
steps.answer: She was not happy in it.
steps.why: She says she was good at it, but she wasn’t happy.
